Reason: Figure 1e shows a left-sided pneumothorax with a chest tube in place, while Figure 1f demonstrates a significantly larger left pneumothorax with lung collapse and subcutaneous emphysema, indicating treatment failure or progression. In Birt–Hogg–Dubé syndrome, recurrent and persistent pneumothoraces are common due to underlying cystic lung disease, often necessitating surgical intervention (such as pleurodesis) to prevent further recurrence.
